news.title: Fifa to offer extra £2.6bn for football development
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino will be standing for re-election in March. Fifa is set to propose a $3.4bn (£2.6bn) increase in the amount of money it hands out for football development across the world. World football's governing body wants to release the money from its reserves in a move which would more than double the level of planned distribution funding for 2027-2030. It says it has been able to release the extra cash because of the commercial success of this summer's World Cup.

news.title: Gianni Infantino faces grilling at potentially ‘explosive’ Fifa council meeting
news.lede: World Cup sell-off, Balogun and peace prize on agenda. Opponents will press home need for independent review. Gianni Infantino will be questioned by Fifa council members over his involvement in the aborted World Cup sell-off plan, the Folarin Balogun affair and the decision to award Donald Trump the inaugural Fifa peace prize at what is expected to be a heated meeting at the world governing body’s headquarters on Thursday. The Fifa president rejected repeated calls for an extraordinary general meeting of council in the summer after the emergence of the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposals, but will meet his critics for the first time since then in Zurich, with one attender predicting that the talks could be “explosive”.

news.title: Football: Soccer-Infantino faces FIFA rebels in Zurich after failed World Cup stake sale
news.lede: ZURICH, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Gianni Infantino faces the soccer ⁠leaders who want him gone on Thursday in his first meeting with FIFA’s top brass since his plan to sell a stake in FIFA ⁠tournaments, including the World Cup, collapsed. Infantino has faced calls to resign from the leaders of three regional football confederations – UEFA (Europe), AFC (Asia) and ‌CONCACAF (North and Central America and the Caribbean) – and their representatives will be present in Zurich for a FIFA Council meeting. They will be joined by their counterparts from Africa, South America and Oceania. On the agenda will be a discussion of the failed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which Infantino was forced to abandon within days of announcing it in July.

news.title: Are the European Women's World Cup play-offs working?
news.lede: England have lost just once this year but have still not qualified for the 2027 Women's World Cup. The ease in which England saw off Greece in round one of the Women's World Cup qualifying play-offs showed just how inefficient the structure currently is. The two-time European champions were superior in every sense as they won 8-1 on aggregate against a Greece side ranked 55 places lower in the world. Realistically, Greece stood little chance in a two-legged tie against Sarina Wiegman's side despite performing well in their home 3-1 defeat.

news.title: AP: FIFA to propose $6,3 billion for soccer development
news.lede: Fifa estimates revenue of approximately $15 billion in the 2022-2026 cycle. FIFA will propose a $6,35 billion development fund to its member associations for the next four-year cycle, including an increased $25 million for each national association, the Associated Press reported today. This information was confirmed by two people familiar with the plan, as well as a letter seen by the AP. FIFA planned to use the financial success of the last World Cup to increase investment in the sport among FIFA's 211 member associations, confederations and other stakeholders.
